event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: HAS’s 2023 filing treats COVID-19 as an ongoing, material threat that has already affected multiple parts of the enterprise and may continue to do so.  The language spans (i) confirmed, realized impacts – higher freight and material costs, manufacturing shutdowns, disrupted film releases, lost sales – and (ii) forward-looking exposures – continued supply-chain fragility, changing consumer demand, remote-work labour dynamics and entertainment monetisation risk.  Statements are largely specific (naming factories in China/Vietnam, port congestion, box-office reliance) and use strong qualifiers such as “significant disruption”, “substantially harm” and “lost sales”, evidencing a high-severity posture.  Because the WHO declaration (March 2020) is less than three years before the 22-Feb-2023 filing, the Time-Decay Principle allows elevated scores (up to 10).  Nevertheless, most disclosures remain un-quantified and partly forward-looking, so individual snippet scores fall in the moderate-to-high 4-6 range rather than the maximum.  Overall, COVID-19 remains a contemporaneous, direct risk driver across HAS’s supply chain, cost structure and revenue channels, warranting sustained investor attention.

evidence_list.snippet: Similarly, as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, some film releases continue to go direct to streaming channels as opposed to theaters or at the same time as theaters or have gone to streaming channels after only a short period of time in the theaters.

components.reason: Explicit causal link to COVID-19 (‘as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic’).
Describes a concrete operational shift (films bypassing theaters) that can undermine traditional revenue streams.
Indicates the change is ongoing (‘continue to go’).
No dollar amount or quantified magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows an ongoing, pandemic-driven change in distribution that threatens revenue, but lacks quantification, yielding a moderate risk score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Technological as well as other changes caused by the pandemic have caused significant disruption to the retail distribution of entertainment offerings and have caused, and could in the future cause, a negative impact on sales of our products and other forms of monetization of content, especially those which are reliant on box office success.

components.reason: Links pandemic to ‘significant disruption’ in retail distribution.
Explicitly flags negative sales impact, present and future.
Highlights vulnerable revenue segment (box-office–dependent content).
Impact unquantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Cites pandemic-driven distribution disruption and sales threat with strong language, but without numbers, earning a score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced increases in material costs and shortages for some of our products, due in part to higher wages being paid due to labor shortages in China and Vietnam, as well as periodic and unpredictable manufacturing shut-downs or slow-downs due to COVID-19.

components.reason: Uses past-tense ‘have experienced’, confirming realised impact.
Details specific cost drivers (labour shortages, shutdowns) directly tied to COVID-19.
No monetary quantification provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct evidence of cost inflation and supply shortages caused by COVID-19; high specificity but unquantified, leading to a score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Given that our toy and game manufacturing is conducted by third-party manufacturers, health conditions, such as the coronavirus, and other factors affecting social and economic activity where our manufacturers are located may affect the movement of people and products into and from those locations to our major markets, including North America and Europe.

components.reason: Identifies coronavirus as a potential disruptor of product movement.
Highlights dependence on third-party manufacturers and cross-border logistics.
Forward-looking ‘may affect’ indicates uncertainty rather than realised loss.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows structural exposure of Hasbro’s supply chain to COVID-related health conditions; risk is potential rather than realised, giving a moderate score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: Natural disasters or health pandemics, such as COVID-19, impacting our manufacturers had and can have a significant negative impact on our business.

components.reason: Acknowledges both historical (‘had’) and prospective (‘can have’) impact.
Uses strong severity phrase ‘significant negative impact’.
Generic statement without operational details or figures.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong wording confirms materiality but lacks specifics, resulting in a score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: The global coronavirus outbreak or other similar outbreaks of communicable infections, diseases, or public health pandemics in the markets in which we and our employees, consumers, customers, partners, licensees, suppliers and manufacturers operate, could substantially harm our business, revenues and profitability.

components.reason: Explicitly states potential for ‘substantial’ harm to business, revenues and profitability.
Covers broad stakeholder base and global footprint, widening exposure.
Purely forward-looking with no cited past impact or metrics.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights breadth and severity but remains entirely prospective and generic, giving it a lower score of 3.

evidence_list.snippet: The global outbreak of the coronavirus which continues to adversely impact global populations, and any other variants or outbreaks of communicable infections, diseases or other adverse public health conditions in markets in which we, our employees, consumers, customers, partners, licensees, licensors, suppliers and manufacturers operate, has had and could in the future have a significant negative impact on our business, revenues and profitability.

components.reason: States that COVID-19 ‘has had’ a significant negative impact – confirmed past effect.
Warns of continued future impact.
References impact on business, revenues and profitability (financial dimension).
No numbers or concrete examples.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mixes realised and forward risk with explicit financial harm but without quantification; earns a score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The occurrence of these types of events can result, and in the case of the coronavirus has resulted in, disruptions and damage to our business, due to, among other things: • difficulties in shipping and distributing products due to ongoing port capacity, and labor, shipping container and truck transportation shortages, resulting in higher costs for both ocean and air freight and delays in the availability of products, which can result in delayed sales and in some cases result in lost sales;

components.reason: Confirms realised impact (‘has resulted in’).
Details concrete operational consequences (shipping shortages, higher freight costs, delayed/lost sales).
Links directly to coronavirus.
No monetary scale provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly specific description of past COVID-driven logistics disruptions and lost sales merits a strong score of 6 despite lack of dollar figures.
